stemBlocks.value: Using a scale of 1 cm to represent 1 unit on both axes, draw the graph of y = 4 for −5 ≤ x ≤ 5.
Think first: The equation says nothing about x, which is the clue to the shape of the line.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p067-q01 from workbook page 67.

contentBlocks.value: y = 4 places no condition on x, so x may take any value from −5 to 5

solutionSteps.instruction: Set up the axes to the given scale.

contentBlocks.value: 1 cm to 1 unit on both axes, x from −5 to 5 and y from −5 to 5

solutionSteps.instruction: Plot the points and join them with a straight ruled line, extending to x = −5 and x = 5.

contentBlocks.value: Result: A horizontal line 4 units above the x-axis

strategyBlocks.value: Recognise that y = 4 fixes the y-coordinate for every point, plot two or three such points across the given range, and join them.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: A horizontal straight line passing through (0, 4), drawn from (−5, 4) to (5, 4) and labelled y = 4.

whyThisWorks.value: Every point on a graph must satisfy the equation of that graph. Since y = 4 imposes a condition only on y, the set of points that satisfy it is every point whose height is 4, whatever its x-coordinate. That collection of points forms a horizontal line, and its gradient is zero because the height never changes as you move along it.

commonErrors.misconception: Drawing a vertical line through x = 4 instead of a horizontal line through y = 4.

examTip.value: Read the equation as a rule about one coordinate: y = a number gives a horizontal line, x = a number gives a vertical line.
